correspondence.component_scope: Initial open dryland east of FM1111, the westward bend across the road and the turn north.
correspondence.finding: The southern detail shows the chosen opening on the gently sloping floor north of the higher Round Mountain and mesa setting. The westward approach and northwest bend occupy the same open low ground, then turn into the valley west of the road. Surrounding contours and relief establish the ordinary receiving connection; no separate basin or intervening ridge transfer is required. No channel name is directly established here.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward valley west of Black Hills, the Gunsight Road vicinity and the crossing toward Baylor Road.
correspondence.finding: The mapped valley stays between the western low escarpments and the higher Black Hills-side terrain. Its receiving floor continues north past the road crossings, shifting from west to east of FM1111. Small mapped tanks and ponds are local features beside the route, not a required lake-to-feeder chain. The selected broad valley passage is supported without assigning a presently wet thread.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: FM1111/Frederick Road valley north to the Scratch Road vicinity.
correspondence.finding: Detailed contour and relief mapping depicts one northward low corridor between the bordering higher ground. The route passes the Frederick Road and Scratch Road settings and local tank/pond surroundings. Continuous valley-floor correspondence is established; no managed canal operation, tank overflow or current culvert performance is inferred.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward bend across the open plain, followed by the northward approach east of Antelope Hills.
correspondence.finding: The southern and northern views overlap across the broad dry receiving floor. The selected eastward bend stays north of the Black Mountains and then turns north on the low plain east of Antelope Hills. The contours and continuous open terrain establish the fan/plain connection at useful geographic scale. The nearby Blanco Draw label is on a different western map context and is not sufficient to name this selected corridor.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward low passage, east/northeast turn and the US62 crossing toward the terminal plain.
correspondence.finding: The northern original shows a low passage between higher contour-defined ground, opening northeast through shallow dissected terrain to the lower plain. The selected route follows that receiving corridor, crosses US62 and continues north on the uninterrupted low floor toward Ranch Road1576. There is no mapped interbasin ridge barrier or missing lake transfer along this ordinary geographic passage. Sparse blue channel linework does not imply a geographic gap.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Northern approach past Ranch Road1576 and the interior of the mapped Salt Basin playa.
correspondence.finding: The low plain continues directly into the southern margin of the large mapped playa labeled Salt Basin. Parts19–20 extend within its floor and finish in its interior. The source endpoint retained by the core metadata and the rendered endpoint were considered separately; they coincide in the same mapped playa. The last stored position is also in that setting. No onward outlet, perennial river channel or current inundation state is asserted.
correspondence.part_index_basis: Zero-based stored part indices within the selected fragment.
